title: Tuning & Simulation Playgound — UI Scrapbook and Grooming
body:
Context and goals:

This is a working notebook for the Optimize -> Recommendations UI focused on an interactive Tuning & Simulation playground. The goal: give engineers and product owners a fast way to preview the impact of batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization choices on latency/cost/quality before applying recommendations to a route or rollout. This doc captures wireframe sketches, interaction notes, and a prioritized backlog for an MVP playgound.

Audience:
- Platform engineers validating tradeoffs
- ML engineers onboarding model variants
- Product owners/PMs approving recommended presets

Top-level user story (MVP):
As an engineer, I want to tweak batching, cache, and quantization presets and immediately see simulated per-token latency, cost estimate, and a quality delta so I can choose a safe preset to apply to a route.

High-level requirements (MVP):
- Single-screen sandbox with three panels: Controls, Simulation Results (metrics + timeline), and Output Preview (example prompts + model responses).
- Support presets + manual override for: batching (max batch size, max wait ms, priority tiers), caching (prefix length, key TTL, hit-rate slider), quantization (bits, backend profile).
- Simulation engine: lightweight deterministic estimator (no real model invocation) using historical token distributions + kernel latency profiles.
- Show conservative error bands and a simulated quality score (synthetic BLEU-like heuristic + embedding-similarity delta).
- Export preset as JSON / apply to route / save as draft.

Wireframe notes (sketch):
- Header: Route select dropdown | Model variant select | Save / Apply buttons | Run Simulation CTA

- Left column: Controls (accordion)
  - Presets: Recommended (cost-saver, latency-fast, balanced), Custom (name, save)
  - Batching:
    - checkbox: enable batching
    - slider: max batch size (1-1024)
    - numeric input: max wait (ms)
    - dropdown: batching strategy {fifo, priority, adaptive-by-latency}
    - small helper text: "Estimated batching efficiency based on traffic shape"
  - Caching:
    - checkbox: enable prefix/KV cache
    - slider: prefix-length (1-256 tokens)
    - slider: TTL (s)
    - toggle: cache shard isolation per customer
    - checkbox: simulate warm cache (pre-populate hits)
  - Quantization:
    - radio: quant level {fp16, int8, int4}
    - dropdown: backend profile {cuda-ops, custom-kernel, x86-optimized}
    - tooltip: "quality risk" with example failure modes
  - Advanced toggles: KV reuse window, dynamic fallback threshold, prefix-embedding cache

- Middle column: Simulation Results summary card (real-time updates)

- Key metrics line: QPS, mean latency (ms), p95/p99 latency, estimated cost / 1M tokens, throughput tokens/sec
- Visual: small stacked bar showing token distribution between fresh gen, cache hits, cached-serving tokens
- Timeline chart: simulated latency over 1h given current traffic shape selection (traffic knob: steady, bursty, diurnal)
- Quality panel: synthetic quality delta vs baseline (green/yellow/red bands) + confidence interval text
- Explainability: list of top 3 impact drivers (e.g., "Batching reduces token cost by 22% but increases p99 by 15ms")

- Right column: Output Preview

- Prompt selector: sample prompts from real eval set (support upload custom list)
- For each prompt: baseline output (model variant, no optimizations) vs simulated output (with current knobs). Show token-level highlights where quantization likely changes tokens (low confidence markers).
- Toggle diff view / side-by-side / blended scoring

Interaction flows & microcopy:
- Run Simulation button should be non-blocking and show progressive estimates as the estimator refines (fast skylight -> finer pass).
- Warn before applying presets that degrade quality beyond a threshold (default 2% quality delta). Warn with explicit example prompt showing degradation.
- Save as preset modal: name, visibility (org/private), apply to route dropdown, optional note.
- Quick compare: allow selecting two presets and seeing side-by-side simulation cards.

Simulation engine assumptions (notes for eng):
- Uses historical traffic histograms (token counts per request) for the route. If not available, default synthetic profiles: steady, p95-bursts, conversational (many short requests).
- Kernel latency table keyed by model-variant + sequence-length buckets, derived from perf bench microresults (see linked_artifacts).
- Cache hit model: hit_rate = f(prefix_length, TTL, traffic_repeat_rate). We should expose adjustable "traffic_repeat_rate" knob for advanced testing.
- Quantization quality model: per-layer sensitivity proxy aggregated into a scalar quality delta estimate. Conservative by default (bias towards underpromising quality).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- User can configure controls and get a simulation result within 3s for small profile and 12s for long refinement.
- Exported preset JSON matches existing runtime config schema (fields validated).
- Guardrails: UI prevents applying a preset that reduces quality beyond configured warning threshold unless explicitly acknowledged.
- Telemetry events emitted: preset_viewed, simulation_run, preset_saved, preset_applied (include knobs snapshot).

Backlog (prioritized):
1) SIM-001 Playground MVP (priority: High, estimate: 8)
   - implement UI scaffolding + estimator integration (fast pass only)
   - connect to model kernel table
2) SIM-007 Preset Comparison view (priority: Medium, estimate: 5)
   - two-column compare + quick-diff
3) SIM-003 Export / Apply Preset flows (priority: High, estimate: 5)
   - save to config store, apply to a route with canary rollout options
4) SIM-005 Output-level confidence highlights (priority: Medium, estimate: 8)
   - token-level confidence overlay using quantization sensitivity map
5) SIM-009 Traffic profile editor + shareable profiles (priority: Low, estimate: 3)
6) SIM-011 Auto-suggest presets (priority: Medium, estimate: 8)
   - ML model that recommends presets given route history (seed with heuristics)
7) SIM-020 Multi-route batch optimization (priority: Lower, estimate: 13)
   - simulation across route groups and shared capacity

Open questions / risks:
- How accurate is the quantization quality estimator? need research + small eval set to calibrate. Who owns that (research or applied-ml)? Action: assign to Omar to prototype a small eval harness.
- Privacy: can't surface real customer prompts in previews for orgs that disallow sample export. Need privacy-aware masking and a per-org opt-in. (Legal check required)
- Performance: running many simultaneous simulations for bulk compare could spike cost. Limit to N active simulations per org.

Notes from sync (2025-02-11):
- PM Ravi: prefer immediate value for SREs — show cost delta and simple "safe" presets first.
- Designer Maya: will produce 3 detailed mockups (MVP default, Compare mode, Preset modal) by 2025-02-20.
- Eng Luis: will expose a test-only endpoint for kernel latency lookups; estimation engine can live as a microservice behind the console.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Maya: initial mocks (due 2025-02-20)
- [ ] Omar: prototype quantization quality estimator + small eval set (due 2025-03-01)
- [ ] Ravi/Eleanor: define "safe" thresholds and notification wording (due 2025-02-18)
- [ ] Luis: stub perf table endpoint + example data (due 2025-02-25)

Conversation references:
- Slack: #prod-optimize thread link (see Linear ticket RED-1203)
- Bench PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimectl/pull/341 (kernel latency metrics)

Edge-case UX ideas (future):
- Simulate mixed model routing where a small % of traffic goes to a larger model as fallback (hybrid routing).
- Show dollar-per-1000qps heatmap across regions when quantization changes memory footprint.
- Inline A/B test setup: run simulation, then create canary rollout that measures real quality on labeled prompts for N days.

Bottom line: the Playground should be an approachable, low-friction place to understand tradeoffs quickly and safely commit optimizations. Keep the first iteration conservative (few knobs + strong guardrails) and iterate with real SRE/ML feedback.

Draft versions and iterations log:
- v0.1 (2024-11-07) initial sketch and feature list (this file)
- v0.2 (2025-01-15) added metric definitions and backlog; changed simulation threshold heuristics
- v0.3 (2025-02-12) incorporated design sync notes, split compare as separate epic
